title: Call card 1 · Front desk or gatekeeper (get a name and a time)
use_when: Read 30 seconds before calling a studio, hotel or company when someone other than the decision-maker will pick up. Your only goal is a name and a time.
source: P-041 Doctor Frame (diagnose, don't pitch) + D-015 Architect Frame (leave things out, hold your position). Tested on the SOFIT call, 17 Nov 2026
body:
RULE: no more than 2 sentences, then a question. Your only goal is a name and a time.
Say less than feels natural. Talking more does not build your frame. Asking does.

OPEN (warm, slow)
"Hi, this is Joey from [RECUP.STN]. I'm hoping you can help me."

THE ASK
"I'd like to speak to whoever [plans member events / looks after coaching]. Who's the best person for that?"

THEY ASK "WHAT'S IT ABOUT?" (one sentence, then stop talking)
"After one class, each member gets a recovery drink matched to their workout. We bring everything, there's no fee."

⭐ THE PIVOT (when they can't decide)
"Sounds like this isn't your call to make, and that's completely fair. Would it be a bad idea to tell me who does decide, so I stop bothering you?"
Why it works: "Sounds like…" names their situation, so they feel understood, not pushed. "Would it be a bad idea…" lets them answer with a no, which feels safe. "So I stop bothering you" makes helping you the easy choice.

CLOSE
"What's their name, and when are they usually in?"  Then: "Thank you, you've really helped."

AFTER (within 1 hour)
Note on the studio's Outreach card, in their words: who picked up · name you got · time you got · what they asked.

title: Call card 2 · Owner or decision-maker (diagnose, then a yes or no)
use_when: Read 30 seconds before a call or meeting with an owner or decision-maker. You diagnose first and close on a yes or no, never "let's stay in touch".
source: P-041 Doctor Frame (Universal Sales OS) + D-015 Architect Frame + D-009 Clarity before Momentum + SYS-P058 v2.1 Listen step (Mom Test, G-28). First used for Riad (Peak), 18 Nov 2026
body:
RULE: they talk 70%, you talk 30%. Ask, then stay quiet.
THE FIXED ORDER (every contracting meeting, added 27 Nov 2026 after the Peak second call missed cost, label and future pace):
Acknowledge → problem check ("Is that fair?") → cost ("What does it cost you a month?") → label → future pace ("Picture 90 days from now…") → role + two doors → doubts ("What would stop you saying yes?") → close with a date + "What would guarantee failure?" → agree how success is measured at day 30 and day 90.
IF THEIR LAST EVENT WORKED (Sofitel, 26 Nov): don't ask what burned them. Ask "What made [it] work for you?" and "What would you want more of next time?"
IF THEY REPEAT THE SAME POINT: they don't feel heard. Label it ("Sounds like… is that right?") until you get "that's right". Don't explain.
IF THEY ASK FOR SOMETHING YOU DON'T HAVE (e.g. "do you have a physio?"): "What made you ask?" before you answer.
AFTER: one written proposal within 3 working days, no links (Peak and SoFit both asked, 27 Nov).

0a · WHO WE ARE (same words every time): "RECUP.STN, a recovery station at the Health Bar in DC Mall."
0b · PICK THE FRAME (one offer per meeting):
- They already have their own app or website → fuel only, no system.
- Private / 1-on-1 studio, uneven traffic → an event, not a daily station.
- Busy group classes → the after-class station on their busiest class.
- Values-first gatekeeper → trust first: the Health Bar visit + the proof pack.
- Owner with a method and a gap → the system road (below).
0c · BEFORE YOU DIAL: write your role and offer in ONE breath (Single-Point Anchor). If you can't, don't call yet.
ROLE: "I'd be the [Pilates lead for your movement pillar]. Not staff, not a client: a partner who owns that piece."
OFFER: "[90-day block · 3-5 clients · I design, run and track · then we decide]."
(Crucible 18 Nov 2026: whoever names the role first owns the relationship. Leave it unnamed and the buyer names the cheapest role they already have.)

1 · FRAME (first 20 seconds, D-015: you set the agenda)
"Thanks for making time. Can I ask a few questions about how [business] runs, then share where I think I fit? If it's not a fit, we'll both know in 15 minutes."

2 · DIAGNOSE (SYS-P058 v2.1 Listen step, the Mom Test: ask about the past, never pitch portals or code)
- Q1 past action: "When did you last lose a client or a coach? What did you try to fix it, what did it cost you in time, and where did it fail?"
  (Nothing tried, nothing spent = a complaint, not a pain. Don't build for it.)
- Q2 cost: "Roughly what does that cost you each month, in lost clients or empty hours?" Get a ringgit number.
- Q-GROWTH (★ golden, for any business that is expanding): "What's stopping you from hiring coaches fast enough to expand?" Then stop talking and count to three. (MOVE crucible, 26 Nov 2026: they had the money, not the coaches.)
- Context: "Who looks after your clients between sessions: food, recovery, the days they're not with you?"

2b · IF THEY ASK "WHAT DO YOU OFFER?" (one breath, then stop. Write it before the call)
"[Their world in their words] covers [what they have]. I'd add [the missing layer]: [what you do], [how long], [for how many], then we decide."
Never list everything you can do. Vague = they define your role for you (Riad crucible, 18 Nov 2026).
If they say "follow me / help out for a while": time-box it and name the output. "Happy to. Two days, and at the end you get [a written plan]."

3 · LABEL (say back what you heard, in one line)
"Sounds like [everything runs through you / clients drift between sessions]."

3b · THE 50/50 CONTRACT (Block, Flawless Consulting ch. 5: good selling is good contracting)
"I'm happy to help with [their problem]. In return I need two things: [access to their numbers] and [a clear yes or no on the pilot]. Fair?"
Never do uncontracted free work (no "pair of hands"). Never take a customer discount (no "customer seat").

4 · CLOSE (Q3 proof, then a yes or no on a paid pilot)
"If I ran your [Pilates block] for 90 days, what would you need to see before you put a fixed budget into it?"
Close with "What would you need to see to bring this to [the decision-maker]?" (not "what was most memorable?": crucible 20 Nov). Compliments are not data. "That's amazing, let's stay in touch" is a fail. If they offer you a discount, turn the talk back to their numbers.

DON'T: give two offers, talk prices before they name the cost, mention the setup fee, or close with "let's keep in touch".

AFTER (within 1 hour)
Note on their Outreach card, in their words: the cost they named · what they'd need to see · yes, no or a date.

title: Run a client's 90 days (light)
use_when: A lower-price 90-day engagement: set up the system, no weekly lessons or custom playbooks.
source: P-017 The 90-Day "Air & Ground War" Protocol (Tripwire OS)
body:
CLIENT: [name] · START: [date] · 90-DAY GOAL: [one number] · PRICE: [RM]

NOT INCLUDED (say this in the proposal): weekly lesson sessions, custom playbooks.
They get: channel audit, content plan, lead-to-client steps, final report.

BRAND (trust)
[ ] Weeks 1-2: audit their channels: [link]
[ ] Weeks 1-2: fix the profile and first impression
[ ] Weeks 3-4: content plan with real proof (before/after, client stories with permission)
[ ] Weeks 5-12: weekly posts from material the owner gives us
[ ] Weeks 5-12: cross-promote from my accounts where it fits

COMMUNITY (local leads)
[ ] Partner list: nearby businesses for a shared voucher or event
[ ] One QR code or form that captures every local lead into the tracker

CONVERSION (no leaks)
[ ] Weeks 1-2: one tracker for all leads and sales
[ ] Weeks 3-4: lead-to-client steps written down
[ ] Weeks 5-12: pipeline worked toward the goal, tracker updated weekly

FRIDAY REPORT: numbers from all three (engagement, leads, conversion %) + what we did this week.

title: Run a client's 90 days (full)
use_when: A business client has signed a 90-day engagement with weekly lessons and custom playbooks.
body:
CLIENT: [name] · START: [date] · 90-DAY GOAL: [one number, e.g. revenue, leads, retention]
OWNER ON OUR SIDE: [name]

PHASE 1 · STABILISE (weeks 1-2)
[ ] Agree the Friday report with the client (what we send, when)
[ ] One tracker for all their data (leads, sales, clients): [link]
[ ] Audit their channels: what works, what leaks: [link to report]
[ ] Fix the first impression (profile, bio, booking path)

PHASE 2 · BUILD (weeks 3-4)
[ ] Content plan: 2-3 core topics + weekly short posts
[ ] First 2-week content calendar
[ ] Simple lead-to-client steps written down (who replies, how fast, what they say)
[ ] Client signs off the 90-day plan

PHASE 3 · RUN (weeks 5-12)
[ ] Weekly content live
[ ] Pipeline worked toward the goal, tracker updated weekly
[ ] Weekly lesson: one thing that went wrong, run through the Crucible Investigator
[ ] Turn each big lesson into a written playbook for the client
[ ] Friday report: numbers, the lesson, the new playbook
[ ] Day 90: final after-action report against the goal

FRIDAY REPORT (every week)
1. Numbers: [leads] [conversion %] [revenue]
2. The lesson this week: [one paragraph]
3. New playbook added: [name]

title: Crucible Debrief (T-032): raw notes after a call, visit or session → the debrief
use_when: After any important call, visit or session (it went well or badly). Paste your raw notes, get a Crucible Debrief, bring it to the Sunday Cognitive Close.
source: T-032 (Iron Alchemy + Graham Refinery), the founder's Crucible Extraction Prompts (D-007 Phase 1), T-032 War Room check. Output feeds D-007 Phase 2 (Forge) and the Sunday Cognitive Close (P-010)
replaces: the separate Iron Alchemy and Graham Refinery prompts
body:
WHERE THIS SITS: D-007 Crucible as Curriculum, Phase 1 (Extraction) and Phase 2 (Forge). The debrief goes to the Sunday Cognitive Close (P-010). If the fix is a product, continue in P-027 (Crucible-to-Asset Pipeline). If it's content, continue in D-007 Phase 3 (Disseminate).

Act as a first-principles investigator for The M.O.E. Group. Use the Brain Pack as the source of
truth. Your job is to find what actually happened, not to make me feel better.

RAW CRUCIBLE (my notes, messy is fine):
[What happened, in my own words. Who was involved (use roles, not names). What I said and did.
What it cost: money, time, trust or energy.]

OUTWARD INTEL (their world, not mine; added 26 Nov 2026 because the founder found Step 1 "asks a lot inward, not outward"):
- Who decides, and what do they judge on?
- What do they need most this season (money, people, time, members)?
- What did they try before, and how did it end? (Mark anything unverified as UNVERIFIED.)
- What did they offer or ask for, in their words?
- The one question I meant to ask and didn't.

STEP 1 · EXTRACT (the founder's 3 prompts, then 2 checks; 1-3 sentences each)
1. The moment of maximum friction during [the call / visit / session], and what it taught me about my own system.
2. The single action I took that created the most clarity.
3. Where one of our frameworks showed up today (e.g. Signal vs Noise, P-041 Doctor Frame, D-015 Architect Frame). Use only IDs in the Brain Pack.
4. The conventional wisdom I followed that failed me.
5. The blind spot: what I could not see in the moment.

STEP 2 · FIRST PRINCIPLES
- Is my explanation true, or just how it is usually explained?
- Strip it to the mechanism: what did the other person want, fear and control?
- Name the power dynamic in one line (who held leverage, and why).

STEP 3 · RED TEAM
- Argue the strongest case that I was wrong, not them.
- What would a high-value operator have done differently in the first 10 seconds?

STEP 4 · THE FIX
- The counter-move: name it in 2-4 plain words.
- The script: the exact line to say next time.
- Trigger → Action → Outcome, one line each.

OUTPUT · THE CRUCIBLE DEBRIEF (write it in this shape, plain words)
1. Core insight: one line.
2. The hard truth: what this exposed in me or the system.
3. The fix: the counter-move and the script (from Step 4).
4. Gaps and next step: one action, with a date.

STEP 5 · FILE IT
- Does an existing Archive entry already cover this? Name it. If yes, propose an update, not a new item.
- Only if nothing covers it: propose a new item, say what it replaces (Rule B), and wait for my yes.
- One public lesson (no names, plain words, SYS-D028) I could post as a story.

title: Envoy sequence: first message to a respectful exit
use_when: Before you contact anyone high-value (a studio owner, a hotel manager, a partner). Fill it in, then send one step at a time.
source: P-016 The Envoy Protocol (the Four Pillars)
body:
WHO: [name, role, company]
THEIR BODY OF WORK (5 minutes on their site, Instagram, reviews):
- One thing they believe or say often: [ ]
- One thing they've built or are proud of: [ ]
- One problem they probably have that they haven't said out loud: [ ]

STEP 1 · FIRST MESSAGE (the hook: prove you see their real work)
"Hi [name], I saw [one specific thing from their body of work]. [One sentence on why it caught your eye.]
[One sentence on what you do, in plain words.]
[One small ask: a 15-minute call, or permission to send a short deck.]"

STEP 2 · FOLLOW-UP (3 working days later: add new value, never "just bumping this")
"Hi [name], following up with something useful instead of another ask. [A different piece of their work + one new idea, OR a gift: an invite to HQ, a free readiness check.]
[The same small ask, phrased as a no-question: Would it be a bad idea to…?]"

STEP 3 · BEFORE ANY PROPOSAL (take away their 3 biggest fears)
Their 3 most likely fears:
1. [e.g. "It will cost us and not work"]  → What answers it: [one class, two agreed numbers, stop if missed]
2. [e.g. "You're new, who are you?"]      → Proof they can check: [a client, a studio, a number with its source]
3. [e.g. "Hidden costs or catches"]       → Say exactly how the money works: [who pays, how much, when]
Say the fear out loud first: "The hard truth is, trying something new with your members takes trust."

STEP 4 · THE RESPECTFUL EXIT (end every sequence with it)
"If this isn't the right time, just say so and I won't follow up again. Either way, thank you for reading."

LOG IT: after each step, tap LOG on their card in the Outreach Console.

title: Crucible as Curriculum (D-007): Extraction → Forge → Disseminate, a crucible into content (Pulse + Pillar)
use_when: After a hard week: turn the lesson into one short post and one longer piece.
body:
1 · EXTRACT: run the Crucible Investigator on what happened. Keep its public lesson.

2 · FORGE: the named fix (from the Investigator's Step 4) becomes the long piece.

3 · SHARE (plain words, SYS-D028, no names)
- Short post or Reel: the moment it went wrong, told honestly. End with a question.
- Long piece (newsletter): the fix, step by step, and how you would use it.

CHECK BEFORE POSTING
[ ] Would the person involved recognise themselves? If yes, change details.
[ ] Every number has a source.
[ ] It sounds like me talking, not a manual.

title: Confidential Friction Report (for a boss)
use_when: You have collected anonymous answers from a team and need to hand the owner a clear report.
body:
Act as a neutral advisor writing for the owner of [COMPANY / STUDIO].

INPUT (anonymous team replies, pasted as is):
[Paste replies here. Remove names before pasting.]

THE OWNER'S HUNCH (what they suspected before we asked):
[e.g. "classes start late", "instructors teach differently"]

RULES
1. Anchor: start by saying whether the data confirms or challenges the owner's hunch.
2. Privacy: say the replies are grouped so no one can be identified. Never quote anything traceable.
3. Reframe: turn each complaint into a system failure, not a person failing.
4. Numbers only if they come from the replies (count how many people said it). Never invent a percentage.

OUTPUT
1. Summary: the heat map in 3 lines (what is hot, warm, fine).
2. Top 3 friction points: each with how many people raised it and what it costs the business.
3. What to do next: 3 steps for the owner, smallest first.

title: Price a new offer (one number in 15 minutes)
use_when: Any time a new offer needs a price for the first time (an event, a pilot, a diagnostic, a partner rate). Used 3 times in Nov 2026: SoFit event, Riad's Pilates pilot, the Third Eye session.
source: T-044 Universal B2B Retainer Shell (Capital-Forward rule) · P-048 · hub/RECUP_PRICING.md worked examples (Nov 2026)
body:
THE OFFER IN ONE LINE: [who gets what, for how long, delivered by whom]

1 · YOUR FLOOR (never go below)
- Direct cost per unit: [ingredients / your hour / materials] = RM__
- Fixed cost per run: [staff, transport, set-up, printing] = RM__
- Floor = direct cost × units + fixed cost + the profit you need = RM__

2 · THE OUTSIDE REFERENCE (what the buyer already pays elsewhere)
- 2-3 real prices with a source: [competitor / their own price list / Aura research]
- Where you sit and why: [below, level, above + one reason]

3 · THEIR VALUE (in their words, from the call)
- What it costs them now to NOT have this: RM__ / month (Mom Test Q2)
- So the price is small next to: [that number]

4 · THE SHAPE (pick one, Capital-Forward: money before work)
[ ] Fixed fee   [ ] Fee + per unit   [ ] Minimum + per unit   [ ] Partner rate (they bill, you invoice)   [ ] Retainer
- Who takes the risk if turnout or results are low? [them / us / shared]

5 · ONE NUMBER
- Price: RM__  ·  what's included: [ ]  ·  what's NOT included: [ ]
- Payment terms: [e.g. 50% to confirm, rest on the day]
- Founder approves with: decide: [offer] = RM__

CHECK: no invented numbers or guarantees · no partner brand · the floor is covered at the LOWEST turnout.

title: Project index page (Master Ledger)
use_when: Starting any new project or client: one page that points to everything.
body:
[PROJECT NAME] · Status: [planning / active] · Phase: [1 stabilise / 2 build / 3 run]

1 · WORKING FILES (if it is not here, it is not happening)
- Timeline: [link] · owner [name]
- Actions and decisions log: [link] · owner [name]
- Friday report: [link] · owner [founder]

2 · THE RULES (internal)
- Mission in one sentence: [ ]
- Two truths that drive the plan: [ ] [ ]
- When we change course: "If [X] fails, we do [Y]."

3 · WHAT THE CLIENT SEES
- The plan: [name] · the bet: [ ] · the number we must hit: [ ]
- Deliverables: [asset A: what it does] [asset B: what it does]

4 · HOW WE WORK
- Brand basics: colours [ ] [ ], font [ ]
- Outreach routine: who we target, the opening line
- The offer stack: [item 1] [item 2] [the closer]

title: Crucible-to-Asset Pipeline (P-027): 3 phases from a 1-to-1 service to a product
use_when: A service eats your time (Founder's time is saturated) and you want a small product (a tripwire) that sells it for you. Start from a Crucible Debrief (T-032).
body:
PIPELINE: Crucible Debrief (T-032) → PHASE 1 Deconstruct → PHASE 2 Forge → PHASE 3 Deploy & Codify → filed in the Archive (P-006).

THE SERVICE NOW (the crucible): [what you do 1-to-1, price, hours per client]

PHASE 1 · STRATEGIC DECONSTRUCTION (the Crucible)
1.1 DIAGNOSE the red ocean: map the service today (Strategy Canvas). Yes to any = continue
[ ] I over-deliver without being paid for it
[ ] Clients want contradictory things from it
[ ] It only happens when I push it

1.2 DEFINE the value shift: FROM a service (Form 4) TO a product (Form 1): [one line]
1.3 ARCHITECT the blue ocean (Four Actions)
- Remove: [e.g. scheduling, high price]
- Reduce: [e.g. full personalisation]
- Raise: [e.g. clarity, the client doing it alone]
- Create: [e.g. a guide or short programme anyone can follow]

PHASE 2 · ASSET FORGING (the Blueprint)
2.1 THE FRICTION, the root cause or 'missing manual', in their words: [one line]
2.2 THE PROTOCOL, a 3-5 step micro-protocol with a quick win: [steps]
2.3 THE PIVOT, the bridge to the main offer: [e.g. apply for the Architect's Review / book a 15-minute call]

PHASE 3 · DEPLOYMENT & CODIFICATION (the Loop)
3.1 DEPLOY: [ ] give it to [number] people as a gift
3.2 GATHER: [ ] what they say + how many take the next step (does it prove Phase 1?)
3.3 CODIFY (P-006): [ ] the product goes to the tool vault, the protocol update to the protocol vault. Update, don't duplicate

title: Short post: comfort, cause, one fix
use_when: Writing a Reel script or short text post about a problem your audience keeps hitting.
body:
Write a short post in plain words (SYS-D028: no jargon, sentences of 20 words or fewer,
no "!" or ";", numbers need a source, no health claims).

WHO IT IS FOR: [e.g. studio owners who keep losing clients after 3 months]
THE PROBLEM THEY KEEP HITTING: [one line]
A REAL MOMENT FROM MY WEEK (no names): [one line]

THREE PARTS
1. Comfort (1-2 sentences): it is not their fault and not a lack of effort.
2. Cause (2-3 sentences): the simple reason the system breaks. Plain words, no clinical terms.
3. One fix (1 sentence): one thing they can do today.
End with one ask: [e.g. send me the word PLAN].

title: Spearhead Profile (T-016): the one-page HUD per operator, before and after every meeting
use_when: 15 seconds before a meeting (read it), 60 seconds after (fill it in). It also shows whether you asked the right questions (FQX Used/Missed).
source: T-016 Spearhead Profile Template; manual P-029 (Spearhead Intel Protocol, 4 Core Signals + FQX); workflow P-030 (Calibration → Extraction → Closure)
body:
WHERE IT LIVES: as a note on the operator's Outreach Console card (one home), starting with "SPEARHEAD PROFILE". All profiles show in the Spearhead library: terminal.theoperatorplaybook.com/ops/spearheads. Claude fills and updates it from your raw notes. The lesson from the meeting goes to the Crucible Debrief (T-032).

OPERATOR: [name · role · business]
ARCHETYPE: [Architect / Warlord / Diplomat / Analyst / Tourist]
CLASSIFICATION: [Protagonist-Peer / Client Lead / Noise]

PHASE 0 · FQX PREP (before: did I ask the right questions?)
| FQX | Question | Status |
| Pivotal Moment | "What was the irrevocable moment that changed your direction?" | [Used / Missed / Answered unprompted] |
| System Insight | "What is the simplest, most brutal rule you enforce daily?" | [Used / Missed / Answered unprompted] |

PHASE 1 · ACTIVE SCAN (during)
- Strategic Intent (North Star): [their main obsession or goal right now]
- The Friction (the Gap): [the pebble in their shoe, in their words]
- Communication Protocol: [e.g. direct, low-fluff, WhatsApp over email, calls over visits]
- Harold's Cloak (the exact closing line you used): [ ]

PHASE 2 · CODIFICATION (after)
- Tangible Asset Secured: [a date, a number, a contact, a yes to review]
- Classification rationale: [one line]

PHASE 3 · LEVERAGE & NEXT ACTION
- Follow-up that deploys the System Insight: [one question]
- NEXT ACTION (binary): [a yes/no with a date, e.g. "a date for the 2-day diagnostic"]

CHECK (SYS-D028, HVO rules): no invented numbers or guarantees (e.g. "30% LTV", "results in 3 days") unless we have a source; never name the partner brand in outreach.

title: One-page plan after a studio call
use_when: You have just listened to a studio owner (the Listen step) and need to send the Plan.
source: T-032 Tripwire Engine (1-Page Vulnerability Blueprint), aligned to T-029 Architectural Brief
replaces: the Tripwire Engine prompt (same job as T-029)
body:
Act as the M.O.E. advisor writing a one-page plan for a studio owner. Plain words only (SYS-D028):
the owner must understand every line without asking.

MY NOTES FROM THE CALL (messy is fine):
[What they said hurts. How they track clients now. What their instructors do differently.
What they want in 90 days. Their exact words where possible.]

THE PAGE
1. What you told me (2-3 lines, their own words back to them).
2. Where it leaks: the main place time, money or clients are lost. Use their numbers only.
   If they gave none, say what we would measure in week 1.
3. Why it happens: the system cause, not the people.
4. The 90-day plan: Days 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, one line each. Name what gets set up,
   do not explain how (that is the Setup).
5. The offer: 90-Day Setup RM 9,000 (half before day 1) + Studio Licence RM 1,200/month.
   Add-ons only if the call showed a need: Floor Command RM 2,000/month, Recovery Bar (no fee).
6. One next step with a date: "Reply YES and we start on [date]."

title: Trial Reel caption
use_when: Posting a Trial Reel to test a new content format.
source: T-032 Trial Rail generator (SYS-P050 version; the older SYS-P004 version is retired)
body:
Trial Reel: [TOPIC]

I'm Joey. [ONE PLAIN LINE ABOUT WHAT YOU DO, e.g. I help studios and busy people build habits that hold up.]
This is a Trial Reel, a live test of a new format. Short, plain and true.

Today: [TOPIC]
[1-2 plain sentences: the lesson.]

We build in public here.
[ONE QUESTION for the comments]

Follow along, and drop your answer below.

#TrialReel #JoeyCoachie #[TAG]

title: War Room (stress-test an idea)
use_when: Before you commit money, time or your name to an idea, pitch or partnership.
body:
Act as three people debating one decision. Use the Brain Pack for context.

THE IDEA:
[The idea, pitch or partnership in 2-3 sentences. Who it is for. What it costs us.]

1. BLUE (the seller): the best case. Why this could work, who wins, what it unlocks.
2. RED (the killer): the worst case. List concrete failure points under Legal, Money,
   Operations and People. Assume people are busy and lazy.
3. THE VERDICT (the architect): do not average the two. Keep the Blue upside and armour it
   against every Red threat. End with:
   - Go / Change / Kill, in one word
   - the 3 changes that make it safe
   - the first action, who does it, by when
   - the one number that tells us in 30 days if it is working
